extracted.intended_audience: registrants, corporate accountants, CFOs, and financial reporting professionals preparing SEC filings for acquisitions and carve-out or abbreviated financial statements
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and presenting carve-out, abbreviated, and substituted financial statements for acquired businesses under SEC Regulation S-X (including Rule 3-05, Rule 3-13 and SAB Topic 1.B), and for requesting waivers or no-action relief when full statements cannot be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of unidentifiable expenses for carve-out financials
rubrics_metrics.description: When expenses are not specifically identifiable, the registrant allocates expenses based on reasonable assumptions to reflect all expenses of the acquired business in the carve-out financial statements. The SEC staff expects the carve-out financial statements to comply with SAB Topic 1.B.1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reasonable allocation methods (e.g., incremental or proportional cost allocation) when specific identification is not practicable. Explain the allocation method in the notes and include management’s assertion that the method is reasonable. Examples of expenses that may need allocation include officer and employee salaries; rent or depreciation; advertising; accounting and legal services; and other selling, general and administrative expenses. Do not alter historical amounts based on expected future results in audited historical financial statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical income statements should reflect all costs of doing business
rubrics_metrics.description: The staff believes the historical income statements of a registrant should reflect all of its costs of doing business; staff has required subsidiaries to revise statements to include expenses incurred by the parent on their behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If prior financial statements were reported by independent accountants and used externally, presentation that shows income before tax as previously reported followed by adjustments for unallocated expenses, income taxes, and adjusted net income has been accepted. Examples of costs to reflect include salaries, rent/depreciation, advertising, accounting/legal, and other SG&A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of stand-alone cost estimates for related‑party arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Because related‑party agreements are not at arm’s length and may change, the staff has required footnote disclosure, when practicable, of management’s estimate of what the expenses would have been on a stand‑alone basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present the stand‑alone cost estimate for each year for which an income statement is required when such basis produced materially different results. Include rationale and, where applicable, explanation of impracticability to prepare separate financial statements that include omitted expenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to reflect income tax expense and deferred taxes attributable to carved‑out entity
rubrics_metrics.description: Carve-out financial statements should reflect income tax expense and deferred tax assets/liabilities attributable to the carved-out entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the carved‑out entity did not file separate tax returns, registrant should reflect an adjustment in the pro forma financial information to include the effect of income taxes as if the carved‑out entity were included in a consolidated tax return with its parent or on a separate reporting basis, if appropriate. The staff prefers the separate-return basis and may require a pro forma income statement reflecting that basis if historical statements do not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment and disclosure of interest on intercompany debt
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial statements are more useful if they reflect all costs, including interest; however, the staff has not insisted that historical income statements include an interest charge on intercompany debt if such a charge was not previously provided, except when debt specifically related to the operations of the subsidiary and previously carried on the parent’s books will henceforth be recorded in the subsidiary’s books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financing arrangements with the parent must be discussed in a note. Where an interest charge on intercompany debt has not been provided, appropriate disclosure would include an analysis of intercompany accounts, average balances due to or from related parties for each period, and a listing of transactions (e.g., allocation of costs, intercompany purchases, cash transfers) reconciled to intercompany accounts in the balance sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on altering historical audited amounts based on expected future results
rubrics_metrics.description: Although SAB Topic 1.B requires a reasonable estimate of expenses incurred on behalf of a subsidiary to be reflected in the audited financial statements, alterations of actual amounts based on expected future results is not permitted in the audited historical financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure audited historical figures are based on historical facts and reasonable allocations of past expenses; do not adjust historical audited amounts to reflect expected future performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for providing audited abbreviated financial statements (Rule 3-05(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant may present audited abbreviated financial statements for an acquired business when: (i) it is not practicable to provide full financial statements or carve-out financial statements of the acquired business; and (ii) the conditions in Question 10.3.80 are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abbreviated FS consist of statements of assets acquired and liabilities assumed and statements of comprehensive income. They will not include all indirect costs (e.g., overhead) but will include expenses incurred by or on behalf of the acquired business during pre-acquisition periods. If expenses are omitted, the title of the statement of comprehensive income must be modified. Provide cash flow information in a note to the abbreviated financial statements or in unaudited supplemental disclosures to the extent available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five specific qualifying conditions to use Rule 3‑05(e) abbreviated financials
rubrics_metrics.description: To provide abbreviated financial statements, all of the following conditions must be met: (1) total assets and total revenues of the acquired business are 20% or less of seller's totals; (2) the acquired business was not a separate entity, subsidiary, operating segment or division during required periods; (3) separate financial statements for the acquired business have not been prepared; (4) the seller did not maintain the distinct and separate accounts necessary to present the omitted expenses; and (5) it is impracticable to prepare such separate financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all conditions are met, abbreviated audited financials may be presented without SEC relief, though registrants may consult staff for concurrence. Additional considerations apply for oil and gas properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation principles and required notes for abbreviated financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: If permitted under Rule 3‑05(e), presentation principles include: balance sheet may be statement of assets acquired and liabilities assumed; statement of comprehensive income must include expenses incurred by or on behalf of the acquired business during pre-acquisition periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes to abbreviated FS must include: description of omitted expenses and rationale for exclusion; explanation of impracticability of preparing full FS; description of how presented FS are not indicative of future financial condition due to omitted expenses; and information about operating, investing and financing cash flows to the extent available. If certain expenses are omitted, adjust the title to reflect omission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which expenses should be included vs may be omitted in abbreviated statements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Rule outlines certain expenses that should be included (e.g., cost of sales and services; selling, distribution and marketing; general and administrative; depreciation and amortization) and notes other expenses that a registrant could omit (e.g., corporate overhead expense; interest expense for debt not assumed; income tax expense; research and development).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If omitted, explain and justify omission in the notes and adjust the statement title accordingly. Include direct expenses incurred by or on behalf of the acquired business during pre-acquisition periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate whether acquired business would qualify as an operating segment under Topic 280
rubrics_metrics.description: One condition to provide abbreviated financial statements is that the acquired business was not a separate operating segment during the periods required; registrant may need to evaluate whether the acquired business would have qualified as an operating segment under Topic 280 if the seller had been a public company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform an assessment consistent with Topic 280 guidance to determine whether abbreviated presentation is permissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviated financial statements rules for oil and gas property acquisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: For oil and gas property acquisitions, abbreviated financial statements may be provided if the registrant acquires less than substantially all of the assets and liabilities and substantially all of the revenue is generated from oil-and-gas-producing activities, and the qualifying conditions of Question 10.3.80 are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abbreviated FS may consist only of audited statements of revenues and expenses. Must include supplementary disclosures described in Topic 932 (oil and gas), which may be presented as unaudited supplementary information for each full year presented, and must include the disclosures required by S‑X Rule 3‑05(e)(2)(iii) in the notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: S-X Rule 3-13 waiver process and SEC staff authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission (and delegated SEC staff) may permit the omission of one or more required financial statements or permit filing of substitute statements upon informal written request when consistent with investor protection; the waiver process is governed by S‑X Rule 3‑13 and is fact‑specific.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver examples include providing a statement of revenue and direct expenses in lieu of full FS; omitting one or more years of historical FS; or providing audited FS for a shorter time. The SEC will grant waivers only for good cause; generally, the staff will not waive auditors’ reports, audited FS, or timely filing requirements. The staff does not have authority to waive Form 8‑K requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to seek a no-action letter for inability to comply
rubrics_metrics.description: If inability to comply with S‑X Rule 3‑05 cannot be resolved through omission or substitution, registrants can request the SEC staff to issue a no‑action letter; the staff may agree not to recommend action against a registrant solely as a result of noncompliance when the inability cannot be corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No‑action relief is fact-specific and typically used in situations where audited FS cannot be obtained despite reasonable efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: What to include in a waiver request under Rule 3‑13
rubrics_metrics.description: The SEC staff has encouraged registrants to include in waiver requests: all relevant facts and circumstances including key transaction terms; results of all three significance tests and why they are not reflective of relative size; reasoning why the information subject to the waiver is not necessary for investor protection; and explanation of other disclosures being provided to convey necessary information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also provide quantification of estimated expense of compliance if expense is a factor. The FRM includes names of staff members to contact for Rule 3‑13 relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors considered in determining 'unreasonable expense and effort'
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no published bright-line guidance; the SEC staff determines what constitutes 'unreasonable burden or expense' on a case‑by‑case basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors that may be considered include relative significance of the acquisition; circumstances causing inability to obtain audited FS; financial and other costs of compliance; and the ability to provide other meaningful information to investors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff view and remedies when an auditor will not provide a report or consent
rubrics_metrics.description: The SEC generally will not waive the requirement for audited financial statements when an auditor is unwilling or unable to provide a report or consent; in rare circumstances (e.g., hostile takeovers) the staff may grant a waiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrant can attempt to retain a new auditor and have necessary periods reaudited, but reaudit may be impossible if management changed and costs/delays may be prohibitive. If relief is granted and circumstances later change, the registration statement should be amended to include audited FS and auditor’s consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of inability to provide an audit report
rubrics_metrics.description: The SEC staff generally will not take enforcement action against a registrant that cannot provide or obtain an audit report on an acquired entity's financial statements when the impossibility is beyond the registrant’s control; however, this does not permit proceeding with securities offerings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due diligence should ensure ability to obtain audited FS and auditors’ consents. In some cases, the staff may accept post‑acquisition results of the acquired business (included in the registrant’s audited FS) on written request to satisfy requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of missing or materially deficient Rule 3‑05 financial statements on Form S‑3 eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to file required Rule 3‑05 financial statements timely or filing a materially deficient Form 8‑K (for example, missing required Rule 3‑05 statements within the 71‑day extension) can affect a registrant’s ability to use Form S‑3 and other registration effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A filing is not considered timely if materially deficient even if a no‑action letter is obtained. Registration statements cannot be declared effective until audited financial statements for the required periods are provided. Timely filing requirement may be considered met if the SEC has provided a Rule 3‑13 waiver permitting audited FS for fewer periods and those FS are timely filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required periods and basis for statements of assets acquired and liabilities assumed
rubrics_metrics.description: Audited statements of assets acquired and liabilities assumed are to be presented as of the end of each period required under S‑X Rule 3‑05, on the basis of the seller's historical GAAP carrying value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If registrant cannot obtain statements prepared on the seller's historical GAAP carrying value for each required reporting date, the SEC staff may consider presenting a statement prepared on the basis of the registrant's purchase price allocation as of the acquisition date. Registrant would still need to present statement(s) of revenues and direct expenses for periods indicated by Rule 3‑05.
